author: aswallace
body: ## Context closes #517 When attempting to load a URL with malformed JSON, the `Query` and `FileList` components were getting stuck in a loading state and not showing the error to the user. Relatedly, if a user only had a single query and then deleted it, the query panel would also show an eternal loading state because the search params weren't getting removed from the URL (so the `Query` component assumed something was supposed to be loading). ## Changes JSON loading bug: - Adds a try/catch around the `decode` step so we can dispatch an error status to the UI - Checks for reload errors in the Query component so that we stop showing the spinner Deleting only query bug: - Removes query params from URL if there are no more queries left (otherwise, loads the first remaining query in the list) Also fixes styling for the example table that appears when there are no queries loaded ## Testing - Manually tested [the url provided in the tagged issue](https://bff.allencell.org/app?c=File+Name%3A0.5%2CBatch%3ANaN%2CRound%3ANaN%2CDate%3ANaN&source=%7B%22name%22%3A%22flyefish_all-data%22%2C%22type%22%3A%22csv%22%2C%22uri%22%3A%22http%3A%2F%2Flocalhost%3A8000%2Fflyefish_all%2Fdata.csv%22%7D&sourceMetadata=%7B%22name%22%3A%22flyefish_all-cols%22%2C%22type%22%3A%22csv%22%2C%22uri%22%3A%22http%3A%2F%2Flocalhost%3A8000%2Fflyefish_all%2Fcolumns.csv%22), plus a few other intentionally malformed URLs - Added a loading state unit test ## Screenshots ### JSON loading bug Before (stuck in loading) vs after (shows error & stops loading) ### Deleting only query bug Before (query shows loading state forever) vs after (no search params, default empty display) --EDITED for [cd550c9](https://github.com/AllenInstitute/biofile-finder/pull/522/commits/cd550c9c5af2d3f1c2d96c8f4c5d7a66b80f96d9)

author: mergify[bot]
body:
Fixes #14343 

### Summary

This commit fixes UnitarySynthesis. It has a parameter `synth_gates`, which is meant to be a list of gates that are synthesized. However, the previous implementation did not respect this parameter, and only synthesized the gates named `unitary`. This commit fixes this issue by checking if gate's name is in `synth_gates`.

### Details and comments

When a non-default method is specified, the DAG nodes are traversed in `UnitarySynthesis._run_main_loop`. There, the name of the node is checked, and in the original implementation, the operation is synthesized if the name is `unitary`. This PR fixes this condition so that the synthesis takes place if the name is in `synth_gates`.

When the method argument is not given, UnitarySynthesis invokes the rust version of `run_main_loop`, which basically has the same structure. The PR also fixes it.<hr>This is an automatic backport of pull request #14345 done by [Mergify](https://mergify.com).

body:
PR removes the `testcontainers-go` dependency and just uses our usual Docker compose setup for running a Postgres instance used by tests.

Also, flattens the directory structure since this is now its own module.

Includes the `VERBOSE_LOGGING` setting as a config setting that can be handled by `config.DefaultSettings`

Simplifies some test helper methods.

### Breaking changes
- Some packages have been moved which will require clients to update their import statements.
- Some `config` methods now return errors instead of calling `log.Fatal`. Most clients do not call these methods directly, but call higher level functions that already returned errors.
- Hides some previously exported objects and functions. As far as I know, these are only used internally, so clients should not notice.

The existing `torch-opt` compile backend couples torch.compile and cudagraph capture. **What type of PR is this?**
/kind feature

**What this PR does / why we need it**:

This PR makes the disk topology feature only add a disk support label to PV NodeAffinity _if_ a new StorageClass parameter is specified: `use-allowed-disk-topology: true`.

The benefit of this is that GKE can enable the `--disk-topology=true` flag without immediately changing PDCSI's behavior.  The feature becomes available, but not enabled.  Customers can then choose to enable the feature when they are ready, plus they gain the granularity of enabling it for specific disk products at a time.  Since most customers need this for Hyperdisk usage, that allows them to target the functionality to their use case.

I've manually tested this feature.  See the steps recorded [here](https://docs.google.com/document/d/13Mh5kMiTeOp4UwOKtRIG7SCUba8V8werVmI9OUuU-zA/edit?resourcekey=0-RVtQpwoT4dL4m-4BZEKQrQ&tab=t.0).


**Which issue(s) this PR fixes**:

Fixes #

**Special notes for your reviewer**:

**Does this PR introduce a user-facing change?**:

```release-note
Only add disk support topologies if StorageClass parameter is true.  --disk-topology=true flag will no longer be sufficient to invoke the functionality.
```

body:
# Fix Sidebar Implementation for Chrome

This PR fixes the sidebar implementation to properly use sidebar mode in Chrome while keeping popup fallback for Arc browser.

## Problem

The previous implementation had both popup and sidebar configurations in the manifest.json, but the popup was taking precedence over the sidebar. When a user clicked the extension icon, the popup was shown immediately instead of the background.js script having a chance to run and open the sidebar.

## Solution

1. **Removed Default Popup from Manifest**
   - Removed the `default_popup` from the action section in manifest.json
   - This allows the background script to handle the extension icon click

2. **Enhanced Browser Detection**
   - Added a function to detect Arc browser using user agent
   - Improved the feature detection for Side Panel API support

3. **Dynamic UI Mode Selection**
   - Created a `setupUIMode` function to dynamically set the appropriate UI mode
   - For Chrome: Uses the Side Panel API to open the sidebar
   - For Arc: Dynamically sets the popup using chrome.action.setPopup API

4. **Multiple Event Listeners**
   - Added event listeners for runtime.onInstalled and runtime.onStartup
   - This ensures the correct UI mode is set when the extension is installed or the browser starts

## Implementation Details

- The extension now properly detects the browser environment and capabilities
- For Chrome: The extension opens as a sidebar panel on the right side of the browser
- For Arc: The extension falls back to popup mode automatically
- The detection is based on both feature detection and user agent analysis for maximum compatibility

## Testing

The extension was tested in:
- Google Chrome: Now correctly opens as a sidebar panel
- Arc Browser: Still works correctly as a popup

This implementation ensures the extension provides the best experience based on each browser's capabilities.

This pull request introduces a stub implementation for the coder graph, adds environment-based toggling between the stub and the real implementation, and updates the orchestrator to use the new graph structure. It also removes the old coder stub logic from the orchestrator stubs. Below is a summary of the most important changes:

### Stub Implementation and Graph Updates
* Added a new `coder_stub` function and `build_stub_graph` method in `src/coder/graph.py` to define and compile the stub implementation of the coder graph.
* Updated `graph_builder` in `src/coder/graph.py` to dynamically switch between the stub and the real coder graph based on the `CODER_STUB_ENABLE` environment variable.

### Environment Configuration
* Introduced a new `CODER_STUB_ENABLE` environment variable in `.env.example` to control whether the stub or real coder graph is used.

### Orchestrator Integration
* Replaced the old coder stub in `src/orchestrator/graph.py` with the new `coder_graph` and updated graph edges and delegation logic to use the new graph structure. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-b3614d9c697e70a544470fe9cff5f7022d38194fa987a06d16c55fdd75f9a26eR13-R14) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-b3614d9c697e70a544470fe9cff5f7022d38194fa987a06d16c55fdd75f9a26eL85-R87) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-b3614d9c697e70a544470fe9cff5f7022d38194fa987a06d16c55fdd75f9a26eL104-R106) [[4]](diffhunk://#diff-b3614d9c697e70a544470fe9cff5f7022d38194fa987a06d16c55fdd75f9a26eL116-R118)

### Removal of Legacy Stub Logic
* Removed the old `coder` stub function and associated `model_coder_messages` from `src/orchestrator/stubs/__init__.py`. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-4c9de601c17b915fb1bdccbc6197dcc3a4d9053f1b1fc2b58a6824cc7f0661c0L45-L50) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-4c9de601c17b915fb1bdccbc6197dcc3a4d9053f1b1fc2b58a6824cc7f0661c0L101-L113)

These changes improve modularity and allow for easier testing by enabling a switchable stub for the coder graph.

body:
## Summary

Adds a component-level setting which can be used to boolean toggle whether PowerBI Semantic Models should be refreshable from Dagster (making the asset executable) or to opt in a subset of the semantic models by name.

```yaml
type: dagster_powerbi.PowerBIWorkspaceComponent

attributes:
  workspace:
    credentials: 
      token: {{ env('POWERBI_TOKEN') }}
    workspace_id: abcd-1234-abcd-1234
  translation:
    owners:
      - team:analytics
  enable_semantic_model_refresh: true
```


```yaml
type: dagster_powerbi.PowerBIWorkspaceComponent

attributes:
  workspace:
    credentials:
      token: {{ env('POWERBI_TOKEN') }}
    workspace_id: abcd-1234-abcd-1234
  translation:
    owners:
      - team:analytics
  enable_semantic_model_refresh:
    - my model 1
    - my model 2
```

## Test Plan

Update unit tests.

Due to the order that we restored auth, versus sent the Developer Profiles to the Auth LSP, there was a problem. We sent the Developer Profiles before the Bearer Token was setup in the Amazon Q LSP

Ensure that we complete restoring of Auth (pushing the Bearer Token to the Amazon Q LSP). Then restore the Developer Profile, ensuring we show the correct messages if needed.

author: lognaturel
body:
Closes https://github.com/getodk/central/issues/1048

#### What has been done to verify that this works as intended?
Put it on the dev server. Verified that there's exactly one `Cache-Control` header and that it's set as expected.

#### Why is this the best possible solution? Were any other approaches considered?
We could also set the headers here to `private, no-cache`, etc. But then we'd be setting duplicate headers which could drift between nginx and backend. I think it's clearer to make caching headers clearly the backend's responsibility.

Note that this does not set the `Pragma` header for backend. I think we could do away with it altogether because it has been deprecated for a long time.

#### How does this change affect users? Describe intentional changes to behavior and behavior that could have accidentally been affected by code changes. In other words, what are the regression risks?
Backend responses should be cached in private caches. We should get 304s.

#### Does this change require updates to documentation? If so, please file an issue [here](https://github.com/getodk/docs/issues/new) and include the link below.
No.

author: viniciustakedi
body:
# 🚀 Endpoints to map markers

**Add Map Markers Functionality**

## 📖 Description

- **What’s changing?**  
  Introduced a new feature to manage map markers associated with reviews. Added DTOs, service, controller, and schema for map markers functionality, integrated within the existing review system.

- **Why?**  
  This PR implements the feature to handle geolocation data (map markers) and associate them with reviews. This change aims to enhance the user experience by allowing reviews to be linked with geographical coordinates, making the review system more interactive and location-aware.

## 🛠 Implementation Details

- Introduced `CreateMapMarkerDto` to validate incoming map marker payloads, ensuring all required fields (latitude, longitude, reviewId) are provided and correctly formatted.
- Created `UpdateMapMarkerDto` by extending `CreateMapMarkerDto` with partial validation to allow selective field updates.
- Defined `MapMarkersController` to handle HTTP requests related to map markers, including creation, update, deletion, and retrieval operations.
- Developed `MapMarkersService` to encapsulate business logic for map marker operations, including validation of associated review existence.
- Created `MapMarkers` schema modeled in MongoDB to store map marker data with fields like latitude, longitude, and reference to a review.
- Integrated the new `MapMarkersModule` with the main application module and linked with the existing `ReviewsModule`.
- Added unit tests for new services and controllers to ensure robust functionality.
- Removed obsolete `MapPinsSchema` as part of the transition to a new `MapMarkersSchema`.

## 📊 Queries changed

- Implemented MongoDB queries for fetching map markers with pagination and associated review data.

## ⚙️ New envs

- None

## 🔗 Related Issues / Tickets

- None

author: markfreeman-dot-dev
body:
This PR improves the project's `Makefile`, primarily focusing on clarity, robustness, and ease of use:

## Key Changes:
- **New Command `make rebuild-clean`:**
  - Performs a thorough cleanup by removing containers, volumes, orphaned resources, and images (`docker compose down -v --remove-orphans --rmi all`).
  - Completely rebuilds the environment without caching (`docker compose build --no-cache`).
  - Starts up containers fresh (`docker compose up -d`).
  - Ensures a clean, reproducible environment, especially helpful for troubleshooting or ensuring consistency.

- **Path Updates:**
  - Updated the executable paths explicitly:
    - DuckDB execution changed from `./duckdb` to absolute path `/usr/local/bin/duckdb`.
    - Python commands explicitly use the virtual environment (`/venv/bin/python`), ensuring consistent environment isolation and correct execution.

## Benefits:
- Guarantees reproducible builds and runs.
- Eliminates potential environment conflicts or stale states.
- Clarifies script execution paths, improving maintainability and reducing errors.

This commit updates the application name displayed on the device to "FaceCheck UANL" and configures a custom launcher icon.

- Modified `AndroidManifest.xml` to change the application label to "FaceCheck UANL" and updated the icon reference to `launcher_icon`.
- Added the `flutter_launcher_icons` dependency to `pubspec.yaml` to manage the app icon.
- Configured `flutter_launcher_icons` in `pubspec.yaml` to use `assets/images/app_logo.png` as the source image for Android launcher icons.
- Added the `app_logo.png` image to the `assets/images` directory.
- Generated various sizes of the `launcher_icon.png` for different screen densities and added them to the Android mipmap resource directories.
- Updated `pubspec.lock` to include the new `flutter_launcher_icons` dependency and its transitive dependencies.
This pull request introduces several changes to improve the user interface, enhance animations, and add new functionality. The most significant updates include redesigning the splash screen and login screens, introducing a new model for teacher exam data, and refining existing code for better readability and maintainability.

### UI/UX Improvements:
* **Splash Screen Redesign**: The splash screen now includes animations for position, scale, opacity, and color transitions, creating a more dynamic and visually appealing experience. The background color transitions from green to white, and the circle animation has been enhanced with scaling and fading effects. (`lib/screens/animation/splash_screen.dart`, [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-001379e35edd15606b33f2103c9115b3e91066519473b3c2ceecb9cf5c443c6eR2-R71) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-001379e35edd15606b33f2103c9115b3e91066519473b3c2ceecb9cf5c443c6eL35-R141)
* **Login Selection Screen Redesign**: The login selection screen now features a gradient background, improved layout with profile cards for "Student" and "Teacher" options, and a more modern and visually appealing design. (`lib/screens/login/login_selection.dart`, [lib/screens/login/login_selection.dartL9-R142](diffhunk://#diff-3fa54e75cf80b429b30a254cd2bb9971f31d4981efeedd38f2cdfd163fe84953L9-R142))
* **Facial Verification Screen Update**: The facial verification screen has been redesigned with a gradient background, a header card for instructions, and a more user-friendly layout. It also includes updated buttons and loading indicators for better usability. (`lib/screens/login/student_login_face.dart`, [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-4ffb5fcc73b88a76ecab3c202aefb30cf41f83c3f64bf4190efcdb22a83bb6eeL134-R206) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-4ffb5fcc73b88a76ecab3c202aefb30cf41f83c3f64bf4190efcdb22a83bb6eeL159-R280)

### New Features:
* **Teacher Exam Data Model**: Added a new model class `RetrieveTeacherExamsResponse` to handle teacher exam data, including fields for exam details and a factory method for JSON deserialization. (`lib/models/teacher/retrieve_teacher_exams_response.dart`, [lib/models/teacher/retrieve_teacher_exams_response.dartR1-R71](diffhunk://#diff-792fa906d7a3ecdfe91910f1f1ff63f3ae5160b770c935cae1504b723ba72b95R1-R71))

### Code Refinements:
* **Removed Debug Logs**: Debugging print statements have been removed from the facial verification logic to clean up the code. (`lib/screens/login/student_login_face.dart`, [lib/screens/login/student_login_face.dartL82-L84](diffhunk://#diff-4ffb5fcc73b88a76ecab3c202aefb30cf41f83c3f64bf4190efcdb22a83bb6eeL82-L84))
* **Improved Snackbar Messages**: Snackbar messages in the facial verification screen are now marked as `const` for better performance and readability. (`lib/screens/login/student_login_face.dart`, [lib/screens/login/student_login_face.dartL100-R106](diffhunk://#diff-4ffb5fcc73b88a76ecab3c202aefb30cf41f83c3f64bf4190efcdb22a83bb6eeL100-R106))

### Minor Updates:
* **Android Manifest Changes**: Updated the app label and launcher icon in the Android manifest for branding consistency. (`android/app/src/main/AndroidManifest.xml`, [android/app/src/main/AndroidManifest.xmlL3-R5](diffhunk://#diff-63272c98a6330850888e633b43ba4c9decee6431a115e0d2731564838eaa1d1dL3-R5))
* **Initial Route Update**: Changed the initial route in `main.dart` to start with the splash screen instead of the teacher home screen. (`lib/main.dart`, [lib/main.dartL33-R33](diffhunk://#diff-e61eb31d013d12616f5532636a88cfa63631dda8f7829e5424e68542214d1608L33-R33))

These changes collectively enhance the app's visual appeal, improve user experience, and prepare the codebase for future scalability.
